title: The Bear and the Two Travelers
text:
Two men were traveling together along a forest road, and they had promised each other to stand together whatever danger they met. Suddenly a bear came out of the trees in front of them.

One of the men was quick and light. Without a word to his companion he ran to the nearest tree, scrambled up into the branches and hid there. The other man was too slow to follow. Seeing that he could neither escape nor fight, he threw himself flat on the ground, held his breath and lay as still as a corpse, because he had heard that bears will not touch a dead body.

The bear came up, sniffed at him, put its muzzle to his ear and nosed around his face. The man did not move. After a while the bear decided he was dead and lumbered off into the forest.

When it was safe, the first man climbed down and asked with a laugh what the bear had whispered in his ear. "It gave me some good advice," said his companion. "It told me never again to travel with a friend who deserts you at the first sign of danger."
lesson: Watch how people act when trouble comes, not what they promise in good times. Choose friends whose loyalty has been tested, and be that kind of friend yourself.
